judgment.rationale: Both Indicators sit in BASIC 5 (rank 1, same-rank) under Strand 3 Geometry and Measurement, but in different Sub-Strands: B5.3.1.1.3 (Lines and Shapes) asks learners to prove a polygon is regular by measuring sides and angles or by folding/superimposing, while B5.3.2.1.1 (Measurement) asks learners to estimate perimeter with centimetre/metre referents, calculate the actual perimeter of 2-D shapes and compare. Their LCs show substantive but complementary work on the same objects: verifying side/angle equality of polygons versus measuring and summing side lengths in standard units. This is meaningful conceptual coherence around measuring properties of 2-D shapes in metric units, yet neither statement's proficiency is evidenced as supporting success in the other (regularity proof is not required for perimeter estimation/calculation, and vice versa), and same-rank placement provides no substantive developmental direction. Lexical/code/page nomination signals are weak (shared tokens only 'and'/'the'; shared code segments only 'b5','3'; adjacent pages) and do not support a directional claim, so the symmetric relation is the supported judgment. Both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context (including the merged BASIC 5 Grade organizer and the merged Measurement Sub-Strand anomaly) and truncated source evidence with 24 omitted evidence items each, so omitted material could refine but not establish a dependency here.

judgment.rationale: B6.1.2.2.1 (BASIC 6, rank 2) asks pupils to multiply multi-digit numbers by 2 or 3-digit numbers efficiently, under Content Standard B6.1.2.2 in Strand 1: Number / Sub-Strand 2: Number Operations. B5.1.2.4.1 (BASIC 5, rank 1) asks pupils to divide 3-digit numbers by 1-digit numbers efficiently, under Content Standard B5.1.2.4 on division. Both are same-grain Indicators about efficient multi-digit whole-number computation, so they cohere substantively as complementary operation-fluency skills. However, the only permitted developmental direction is second_to_first (division fluency to multi-digit multiplication), and the evidence does not support that: the BASIC 5 statement targets division by a 1-digit divisor, a different operation whose mastery is not shown here to support multi-digit-by-2/3-digit multiplication; if anything the conceptual dependency runs the other way. The nomination rests mainly on rank proximity and surface token/trigram overlap ('digit', 'numbers by', 'efficiently'), which is not developmental evidence. The BASIC 5 endpoint and its parent carry unresolved-ancestry framework-root fallback, so hierarchy was not used as positive evidence; judgment rests on trustworthy statement text, codes, and resolved grade coordinates. relatesTo is therefore the best supported permitted decision.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (rank 1, same Grade coordinate) under the same Content Standard B5.1.3.1 ('strategies for comparing, adding, subtracting and multiplying fractions') in Sub-Strand 3: Number: Fractions. B5.1.3.1.2 targets comparing and ordering fractions (LCs: compare fractions, order fractions), while B5.1.3.1.6 targets using models to explain multiplying a fraction by a whole number (LC tagged models, multiplication, whole number). They are complementary facets of fraction sense within one standard: relational/magnitude reasoning about fractions alongside modelled multiplication. The evidence shows no substantive dependency — modelled fraction-by-whole-number multiplication does not require prior comparing/ordering, and ordering does not depend on multiplication models — and same-rank placement provides no directional support, so a symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment rather than buildsTowards.
